causal_scenarios.population: articles in the journal's back catalogue
causal_scenarios.effect_vp: were cited more often in the following three years
causal_scenarios.alternative_cause: The journal converted its most-requested articles first, and those were already the ones other researchers were seeking out.
causal_scenarios.reverse_causation: Editors chose articles for conversion by watching which ones were accumulating citations fastest.
causal_scenarios.sampling_flaw: The comparison covers the fourteen articles converted in the pilot, all from a single subfield.
inert_facts: The conversion work was carried out by an external contractor the publisher had used for two earlier digitisation projects.
Citation counts were drawn from a database the journal has used for its annual reporting since long before the conversion began.
The journal's overall submission volume rose slightly over the period, in line with the rise reported across its whole subject area.
Open and closed articles are hosted on the same platform and are returned by the same search interface in the same result format.
causal_scenarios.control_comparison: Articles of comparable age and subject that remained closed showed no comparable rise in citations.

ratio_scenarios.base_change: The journal received almost three times as many submissions last year as in the editor's first.
inert_facts: The journal introduced an online submission system between the two years.
Desk rejections are recorded by the managing editor rather than by the reviewers.
The journal's page budget did not change over the period.
The journal's editorial board met the same number of times in each year.
